export-explorer-publish-replaces-both.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: publish() caught every exception, KeyboardInterrupt included, and restored the previous public/data and public/evidence before re-raising. The Rust command cannot catch a signal, because the crate forbids unsafe code, so the Python front ignores SIGINT while export-explorer publish runs: an interrupt in that window no longer stops publication. Compatibility impact: Ctrl-C during the two moves publishes the new export where Python kept the old one; SIGTERM ends both as before. tools/test_export_explorer.py checks that SIGINT is ignored only while publish runs, and the cargo tests a_failed_move_restores_the_previous_pair, a_failed_restoration_keeps_the_backups and a_failed_first_publication_leaves_no_directories pin the restoration.

export-explorer-unsortable-manifestation.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. From local independent review of #198: the v1 case gave its integer claim ids a null family_id, so the export skipped them before sorting and the case pinned exit 0 with no manifestations; it now links both claims to GT-t1 and pins the refusal. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py sorted family manifestations and configuration models with sorted(), which orders any mutually comparable values, such as integers. The Rust export sorts text, as every schema-valid claim id and recorded model is, and refuses two or more values that are not all text with TypeError, exit 1, rather than reproduce Python's ordering of numbers and booleans. A list with one value is kept as it is, as Python keeps it. Compatibility impact: none for schema-valid current facts, under any interpreter; facts edited to hold such values exported in Python and are now refused. On these facts the base export wrote manifestations [1, 2]; the Rust export exits 1 after staging the evidence it reached first.

export-explorer-lone-surrogate-facts.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py kept a lone surrogate escape from a current document as Python text, exported it when no published field held it, and failed with UnicodeEncodeError, exit 1, when one did. The Rust facts reader refuses every lone surrogate escape with ValueError, exit 1, as bench-tools' JSON reader does. In the same way the Python front writes the facts with json.dumps(allow_nan=False), as #198 specifies, so a NaN or infinite number anywhere in the current documents is refused with ValueError, exit 1; Python exported one outside the published fields and refused a NaN inside them as 'staged dataset differs from the export'. tools/test_export_explorer.py pins the non-finite refusal. Compatibility impact: none for the repository; its current facts hold neither, which the full export checks on every build.

export-explorer-evidence-reads-every-inp.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py restored each missing evidence file as the export reached it, so a missing, unrestorable packet failed with 'missing or changed evidence' before a later input was read. export-explorer evidence reads every input before the Python front restores anything, so the unreadable normalized.json fails first, with json's message. A retained-backups refusal likewise comes after restoration. Compatibility impact: when an export has both an input error and missing evidence, the input error is reported and no evidence is restored; an export with either one alone fails as before.

export-explorer-usage-missing-stage.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. export-explorer-unicode-15-1-adjudicatio.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. export_explorer.py's KeyError and other diagnostics quoted input with repr, which followed the running interpreter's Unicode database, so it escaped characters that database lacked. The Rust export quotes with the bench-tools repr, which escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: a quoted value changes when it holds a character assigned after the former interpreter's Unicode version. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0, which 3.12 escapes and Rust writes as-is; none the other way. Older interpreters differ on more: Python 3.13 (Unicode 15.1) on 5,185, the Unicode 16.0 additions, and Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) on 11,130. This case pins U+2EBF0, added in Unicode 15.1, in a claim's adjudication id that no decision has: the base export on Python 3.12 printed KeyError: 'probe-\U0002ebf0'; Rust writes the character, as the base export did on Python 3.13 and 3.14.

export-explorer-abbreviated-options.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Changes accepted input on purpose. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer matched a long option only when spelled in full and refused a prefix such as --ro, --f or --b as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap's infer_long_args expands a unique prefix of a long option, as argparse does; an ambiguous prefix is still a usage error, exit 2. Rationale: #215 asks for argparse-style abbreviations through infer_long_args. Compatibility impact: command lines that spell options in full are unchanged, and a unique prefix that was refused now runs, toward Python: export-explorer has no argparse counterpart. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-dot-digit-facts.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. Supersedes export-explorer-decisions.v6.json's refusal of -.5. Old behavior: clap 4.6.7 read a dash-led argument as a value only when it parsed as a number with a digit before any dot, so --facts -.5 was an unexpected argument, exit 2. New behavior: export-explorer reads a dash-led value as methodology and current-grading read one, through main.rs's attach_dash_led_values: a dash, an optional dot and a decimal digit, or a dash-led argument that holds a space, after an option that takes a value is that value, as Python 3.14's argparse reads it, so the command lists the evidence of the facts file -.5, exit 0. Rationale: export-explorer with no command replaces tools/export_explorer.py, whose argparse took --public -.5 and --public '-published dir', and the commands share export-explorer's options, so one reading covers both. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs; the attached form, --facts=-.5, still works. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-exponent-facts.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Changes accepted input on purpose, toward Python 3.14. Old behavior: a dash-led value holding a letter, such as -1e5, was refused as an option, exit 2, as Python 3.12's argparse refuses it. New behavior: clap 4.6.7 reads -1e5 as a negative number in exponent form and takes it as the value, as Python 3.14's argparse does, which takes any argument that starts with a dash and a digit. Rationale: clap's allow_negative_numbers rule; keeping 3.12's refusal would need hand-written parsing #215 removes. Compatibility impact: a command line that was refused now runs, and no caller passes such a value; export-explorer has no argparse counterpart. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-bare-double-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. export-explorer-help-with-attached-argum.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. Changes the first line of export-explorer's help, which this case pins by prefix, from 'List, stage or publish the explorer export from the current facts tools/export_explorer.py writes' to 'Export the current facts to public/ for the explorer, or list, stage or publish an export from a facts file', because this change deletes tools/export_explorer.py and export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export. Otherwise unchanged from export-explorer-decisions.v6.json: clap reads -hx as -h then -x and prints help, exit 0, as argparse does under Python 3.12 and 3.14. export-explorer-help-with-equals-or-dash.reason: Adopt for #215 slice A, part of #149, under #154's authority: the repository owner allowed pinned crates.io dependencies in rust/bench-tools on 2026-10-19, and #215 replaces main.rs's hand-written option parsing with clap 4.6.7 (derive, infer_long_args), delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. Keeps the exit code and changes the message. Old behavior: bench-tools export-explorer refused -h with = or - attached, such as -h=1, -h=, -h- and -h-x, as an unrecognized argument, exit 2. New behavior: clap would print help for them, exit 0, so main.rs refuses an -h before -- whose attached text, after any further h's, starts with = or - when clap is about to print help, with clap's error: prefix, argparse's message argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1', and the subcommand's usage, exit 2. Rationale: argparse under Python 3.12 and 3.14 refuses these spellings with that message, exit 2, and prints help only for spellings such as -hx, -hhx and -hxh=1, whose attached text after the h's starts with neither. Compatibility impact: none for exit codes; only the diagnostic wording changes. This supersedes export-explorer-decisions.v5.json, which said argparse prints help whenever the text attached to -h starts with neither = nor -; argparse first skips further h's, so it refuses -hh=1 and -hh-x too. Resolving issue: #215.

export-explorer-current-missing-inventor.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. The current inventory is missing and an old bench/scoreboard.json exists: the export reads no archive and is refused, naming the inventory. Old behavior: the front caught no exception from current_grading.load_current, so Python printed a traceback ending 'current_grading.InputError: cannot read <root>/bench/grading/current/inventory.json: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<root>/bench/grading/current/inventory.json'' and exited 1. New behavior: bench-tools prints 'export_explorer.py: current_grading.InputError: cannot read <root>/bench/grading/current/inventory.json: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<root>/bench/grading/current/inventory.json'', the traceback's last line, and exits 1, as every other export failure prints. Rationale: one line per failure, as the export's other diagnostics give it. Compatibility impact: stderr is one line where it was a traceback; the exit status is unchanged. current_grading wraps every read failure the fixtures reach as InputError, so the class name is the traceback's; bench_tools::current_grading keeps no class for an OSError the Python left unwrapped, and names it InputError too. Resolving issue: #234.

New behavior: every attempt detail file carries usageCorrectionUrl, the link to bench/deviations/usage-lower-bounds.v1.json for an attempt that deviation lists and null otherwise; this case's attempts are not listed, so each gains "usageCorrectionUrl": null and no other value changes. Rationale: the explorer links an undercounted attempt's usage correction from its evidence drawer. Compatibility impact: a reader of the detail files sees one more key; src/lib/data.ts types it as a string or null. Resolving issue: #289.

export-explorer-current-unicode-15-1-rec.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. A registry source whose arm ends in U+2FFC and whose configuration is unknown: the record is refused when the export reads it, quoting the (run, arm) key. Old behavior: the front caught no exception from current_grading.load_current, so Python printed a traceback ending 'current_grading.Inconsistent: ('runs/2026-01-01-grade-test', 'codex-high\u2ffc'): unknown configuration' and exited 1. New behavior: bench-tools prints 'export_explorer.py: current_grading.Inconsistent: ('runs/2026-01-01-grade-test', 'codex-high\u2ffc'): unknown configuration', the traceback's last line, and exits 1, as every other export failure prints. Rationale: one line per failure, as the export's other diagnostics give it. Compatibility impact: stderr is one line where it was a traceback; the exit status is unchanged. That last line is Python 3.12's, which CI ran. The key is now quoted through pytext::repr, which escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), so U+2FFC, added in Unicode 15.1, is written as it is, as the front printed it under Python 3.13 and 3.14. A quoted run, arm, target or path changes when it holds a character assigned after the interpreter's Unicode version: against Python 3.12 (Unicode 15.0) on 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0; against older interpreters on more, 11,130 for Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0). No tracked run, arm or target name holds one. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-current-abbreviated-root.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. --r named --root in the front, whose only long options were --root and --public. bench-tools also has the hidden --restore, so clap refuses --r as ambiguous. Old behavior: the front's argparse expanded --r to --root and exported. New behavior: clap refuses --r, exit 2, because it also prefixes --restore, an option of export-explorer evidence. Rationale: the whole export shares export-explorer's options with its commands. Compatibility impact: --ro and longer prefixes still work; bun run data passes no option. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-current-facts-without-co.reason: Adopt for #234, part of #156. bench-tools export-explorer with no command now runs the whole export: it loads the current facts in process through bench_tools::current_grading::load_current and coverage_status, restores the evidence they link, stages, reads the record again and publishes, as tools/export_explorer.py did through a temporary facts file; this change deletes that front, and bun run data runs the command. Diagnostics keep the program name export_explorer.py. --facts with no command: the whole export reads no facts file, so the option is refused. Old behavior: the front refused --facts as an unrecognized argument, and bench-tools export-explorer with no command refused with 'give one command: evidence, stage or publish'; both exit 2. New behavior: no command runs the whole export, which takes only --root and --public and reads BASE_PATH, as the front did; --facts, --base-path, --stage or --restore without a command is refused, naming the option, exit 2. Rationale: the front's command line moves to bench-tools. Compatibility impact: no caller ran export-explorer without a command. Resolving issue: #234.

export-explorer-help-before-invalid-shor.reason: Adopt for #268, part of #156, whose delivery plan ports each Python command line to bench-tools with argparse's arguments and exit codes. bench-tools export-explorer: --help before -h=1 prints the help and exits 0, because argparse acts on --help as soon as it reads it. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: tools/export_explorer.py, deleted in 6bef4fb04, printed argparse's help and exited 0, run from its last revision, where bench-tools refused the later -h=1 with exit 2. New behavior: bench-tools export-explorer prints clap's help and exits 0; main.rs refuses -h, or a run of h's, with an attached = or - argument only when it is the first help before --, for every subcommand. Rationale: argparse acts on the first help it reads, so an earlier --help, or a unique prefix of it such as --hel, wins over a later -h=1. Compatibility impact: the exit code now matches the deleted Python's; only the help wording differs, as for every bench-tools help. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #268.
